etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English pedlere, pedlare, pedeler, alteration of Middle English peddere (“hawker, peddler”), of uncertain origin. Compare Medieval Latin pedārius, from Latin pedāre (“to furnish with feet; prop up”).

definitions.definition: An itinerant seller of small goods.

quote.citation: 1953, Tom Lehrer, “The Old Dope Peddler”, in Songs by Tom Lehrer, Pantheon, published 1981, page 18:
quote.text: Here's a cure for all your troubles  Here's an end to all distress  It's the old dope peddler  With his powdered happiness

definitions.definition: (figurative) A fake-news disseminator; A conspiracy-theory propagator.
